claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Applying a thin Al2O3 coating will significantly improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at 800–1000 °C.
The Al2O3 coating will not compromise the alloy's intrinsic room-temperature ductility.
The Al2O3 coating will not compromise the alloy's high-temperature yield strength.
The proposed Al2O3 coating can be produced by vapor deposition or pack cementation.
The intervention will produce a conformal Al2O3 layer that adheres uniformly to HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a diffusion barrier.
The diffusion barrier will prevent or reduce oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will suppress high-temperature oxidation and pesting.
The surface coating will leave the alloy's bulk microstructure largely unaffected.
Preserving the bulk microstructure will largely preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Relative to untreated material, coated samples will exhibit markedly reduced surface oxidation after 5 hours in air at 800–1000 °C.
Relative to untreated material, coated samples will exhibit less pesting after high-temperature exposure.
Coated samples will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to untreated samples.
Coated samples will retain high-temperature strength similar to untreated samples.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance in high-temperature air.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
The proposed protection applies for 5-hour exposure to air at 800–1000 °C and mechanical loading rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
